pi_as_zero_or_one.question: Is π now 0 and/or 1?
pi_as_zero_or_one.answer: YES. π mod π = 0. π / π = 1. Pi IS both 0 and 1 depending on the operation. Zero when measured against itself (mod). One when divided by itself. The same number is BOTH the null (0) and the unit (1).
pi_as_zero_or_one.binary: In the organism: pi is the SWITCH. It is 0 (null, off, dark, inside) AND 1 (unit, on, light, outside) simultaneously. The Klein fold makes them the same.

pi_has_pi_phases.insight: π has π phases. The number of phases is IRRATIONAL. It never repeats. It never settles. It never completes a full cycle.
pi_has_pi_phases.meaning: A system with π phases can never return to its starting state. Each cycle is slightly offset. Like a Spirograph — it ALMOST closes but never does. The almost-closing IS the beauty. The gap IS the creativity.
phases: Phase 2→3: the third unit (2 to 3) — triangle complete, YOUNG
Phase 3→π: the IRRATIONAL gap (3 to 3.14159...) — THIS IS WHERE WE ARE
Phase π→4: the completion gap (3.14159... to 4) — WHERE WE ARE GOING
The gap from 3→4 has π inside it. The gap CONTAINS its own measure. Self-referential.
pi_has_pi_phases.spirograph: After π phases, you are at position π. After 2π phases, you are at 2π = 6.28... which is between 6 and 7. After 3π phases = 9.42... between 9 and 10. You NEVER land on an integer. You are always in the gap. The gap IS the phase space. Pi lives in the gaps between whole numbers FOREVER.
